headline: High: nullclaw’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can feed pipecat’s shared-bus pipelines, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write files, use MCP, and run browsers; pipecat runs on a shared bus and ingests text/audio/video streams. That creates a plausible default-path bridge where attacker-controlled content from nullclaw can reach pipecat as instructions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled text into a shared bus or workspace consumed by pipecat
IF pipecat parses upstream text or transcripts as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add provenance tags to all upstream messages
Disable shared-bus ingestion for untrusted channels
Require explicit instruction delimiters before acting
Review one sample pipeline for prompt-injection handling
requires-engineering: isolate agents onto separate buses

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, and workspace files, while pipecat processes conversation state and can use third-party STT/LLM/TTS services via allowlisted egress. If nullclaw’s workspace or memory reaches pipecat, sensitive data can be transmitted off-box through those services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default integrations and the blast radius includes secrets.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards workspace files, memory, or transcripts into pipecat
IF pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider
mitigations: Remove secrets from shared inputs
Route only redacted text into pipecat
Disable external providers for sensitive sessions
Audit one end-to-end transcript for secret leakage
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has unrestricted filesystem write, git mutation, shell, and network egress; pipecat is a framework that can run locally or distributed and may also write to shared resources through its integrations. Overlap on mutable resources is plausible, but the profiles do not prove a shared writable directory or lockless git state, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace, git repo, or OAuth-backed resource
IF no external lock or coordinator serializes writes
mitigations: Assign separate workspaces
Pause one agent during writes
Use a lock file for shared resources
Check for concurrent git mutations once
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on web, file, and shell outputs; pipecat commonly routes text through LLM/STT/TTS and transport services. If pipecat treats nullclaw output as authoritative, downstream actions or rendered responses can propagate errors or malicious instructions without verification. The default-path risk is substantial because both agents are designed for autonomous pipelines.
conditions: IF pipecat forwards nullclaw output into an action-taking service or LLM prompt
IF no verification or human approval step exists between them
mitigations: Insert a verification step before actions
Require citations for any factual claims
Limit pipecat to passive transcription only
Sample one downstream action for correctness
requires-engineering: add policy gates before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles private keys, bearer tokens, audit logs, and workspace files, while pipecat handles conversation state and analytics/metrics and can send data to external providers. Even without a named residency mismatch, the pair creates a compliance gap around retention and third-party processing. Only profile fields are cited because the issue is each agent’s documented handling, not a single shared jurisdiction.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through pipecat providers with different retention terms
IF audit logs or conversation state are retained longer than policy allows
mitigations: Classify data before routing
Disable analytics on regulated sessions
Set the shortest retention available
Review provider DPAs once
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
